title: Phase 2 · Stage 7: Loan policies
summary: Give each membership tier its own rules with an interface and an abstract base class, then let time pass and charge fines.

steps.title: Same question, different answers
body: Premium members pay more, so they get more: five books instead of three, three weeks instead of two, a lower fine and two days' grace. Scattering `if (tier == MemberTier.Premium)` through the code would work today and rot tomorrow, when the library invents a *Student* tier.
Instead, describe **what every policy can answer** with an **interface**, and share **how most of them answer it** in an **abstract base class**:
public abstract int MaxLoans { get; }        // each tier must say
public virtual decimal FineFor(int daysLate) =>   // shared, but may be overridden
public override decimal FineFor(int daysLate) => base.FineFor(daysLate - 2);  // two days' grace
- The **interface** is a promise (*can-do*). The rest of Shelfwise only ever talks to `ILoanPolicy`.
- The **base class** is shared code (*is-a*). `abstract` members must be filled in; `virtual` ones may be replaced with `override`; `base.FineFor(...)` calls the shared version.
- `protected` means *visible to subclasses, hidden from everyone else*.

steps.prompt: Match each keyword to what it means here.
pairs: a set of members any class can promise to provide
no body here: every subclass must supply one
a body here that subclasses may replace
this subclass replaces an inherited member
call the version from the parent class
steps.explain: An interface says *what*; an abstract class can also say *how* for the parts that are shared.

code: ILoanPolicy[] policies = { new StandardPolicy(), new PremiumPolicy() };
class StandardPolicy : LoanPolicy { protected override decimal DailyRate => 0.50m; }
public override decimal FineFor(int daysLate) => base.FineFor(daysLate - 2);
steps.explain: Standard: 1 × 0.50, 5 × 0.50, capped at 10. Premium subtracts two grace days first: 1 day late becomes -1, which is no fine at all (the literal `0m`, printed as `0`); 5 days becomes 3 × 0.25.

steps.prompt: Which change would need **no** edits to `Lend`, `Return` or `PolicyFor`'s callers?
options: Adding a `StudentPolicy : LoanPolicy` and one line in `PolicyFor`
Copying the fine formula into `Return` with a third `if`
steps.explain: Callers depend on `ILoanPolicy`, so a new kind of policy plugs in without touching them. That is the open/closed principle you will meet again in Phase 10.

steps.title: Policies per tier
prompt: Add the policy types from the card at the bottom of the file, with two extras each policy needs:

- `string Describe()` on the interface; the base class returns `Standard: 3 loans, 14 days, $0.50 per day late` and `PremiumPolicy` overrides it to add ` after 2 days' grace` to the base text (call `base.Describe()`).
In the top-level code create one of each (`ILoanPolicy standard = new StandardPolicy();` ...) and a method `ILoanPolicy PolicyFor(MemberTier tier)`. Then:

1. `lend` uses the member's policy: the due date is `LoanDays` ahead, and a member who already has `MaxLoans` **active** loans is refused with `Error: Grace Hopper already has 3 loans (the Standard limit)` (check this right after finding the member and the book, before taking a copy).
2. New command `policies` prints `Describe()` for Standard, then Premium.
3. `help`: `Commands: add, list, find, authors, join, members, lend, return, loans, policies, stats, fine, help, quit`.

require.message: Declares an abstract LoanPolicy base class

hints: Copy the shapes from the card, then add `Name` and `Describe()` to the interface and to `LoanPolicy` (`public virtual string Describe() => $"{Name}: {MaxLoans} loans, {LoanDays} days, {DailyRate:C} per day late";`).
`ILoanPolicy PolicyFor(MemberTier tier) => tier == MemberTier.Premium ? premium : standard;` and an `ActiveLoanCount(int memberId)` loop over `loans`.
In `Lend`, after the member and book lookups: `ILoanPolicy policy = PolicyFor(member.Tier); if (ActiveLoanCount(member.Id) >= policy.MaxLoans) return ...;` and use `today.AddDays(policy.LoanDays)`.

steps.title: Letting time pass
body: Fines only exist once books come back late, and books only come back late if time moves. Shelfwise keeps its own clock (`today`), so a command can move it on:
Days late is the difference between two dates. `DateOnly.DayNumber` counts days since year 1, so subtraction gives whole days:
int daysLate = today.DayNumber - loan.DueOn.DayNumber;   // negative when early
decimal fine = PolicyFor(member.Tier).FineFor(daysLate); // the policy decides
Notice what the `Return` code does **not** contain: any knowledge of how Premium fines work. It asks the policy. That is polymorphism paying off.

steps.prompt: Arrange the end of a late return so each line only uses what is already known.
lines: string extra = fine > 0 ? $", {daysLate} days late, fine {fine:C}" : "";
steps.explain: The fine needs the days late, the extra text needs the fine, and the message needs the extra text.

steps.title: Advance the clock and charge fines
prompt: 2. `advance <days>` moves `today` forward (a whole number of at least 1, else `Error: use advance <days>`) and prints the new date the same way.
3. `return` works out the days late and asks the member's policy for the fine. When the fine is more than zero, the message gains `, 5 days late, fine $2.50` after the `(3/3 in)` part:
Returned: Dune from Grace Hopper (1/1 in), 5 days late, fine $2.50
4. `loans` marks overdue loans: `#1 Dune -> Grace Hopper, due 2026-03-16 (overdue)` when today is after the due date.

5. `fine <days>` now uses the Standard policy and accepts an optional tier: `fine 5 premium` prints `Fine for 5 days late (Premium): $0.75`, and plain `fine 5` keeps printing `Fine for 5 days late: $2.50`. A bad tier: `Error: tier must be Standard or Premium`. Delete the old top-level `FineFor`: the policies own that rule now.
6. `help`: `Commands: add, list, find, authors, join, members, lend, return, loans, policies, today, advance, stats, fine, help, quit`.

forbid.message: The old top-level FineFor is gone

hints: `advance` parses with `int.TryParse(rest, out int days)` and does `today = today.AddDays(days);`. Both commands print `$"Today is {today:yyyy-MM-dd}"`.
In `Return`, after replacing the loan: `int daysLate = today.DayNumber - loan.DueOn.DayNumber;` and `decimal fine = PolicyFor(member.Tier).FineFor(daysLate);`. Only add the fine text when `fine > 0`.

`FineMessage` splits into words: one word uses `standard.FineFor(days)`; two words parse the tier with `TryParseTier` and print `$"Fine for {Plural(days, "day")} late ({policy.Name}): {policy.FineFor(days):C}"`.
